title: Report: The town library
text:
Report on the future of Riverside Library

Introduction
Visitor numbers at Riverside Library have fallen by 30% over the past five years. The library committee asked for this report to find out why people visit less often and what could be done to attract them back. The findings are based on a survey of 350 local residents, both users and non-users of the library, and on interviews with staff.

Why people visit less
The most common reason given by former users was that they now read e-books or listen to audiobooks at home (42%). A quarter of respondents said that the opening hours were inconvenient: the library closes at 5 p.m. on weekdays and is closed on Sundays, which makes it difficult for people who work full-time to visit. Others mentioned that the building feels old and uncomfortable, with not enough seating and a slow internet connection.

What people would like
Interestingly, the survey showed that many residents still value the library as a place, not only as a source of books. Over 60% said they would visit more often if the library offered events such as author talks, language clubs or children's workshops. Young people in particular asked for a quiet space to study with reliable Wi-Fi, while older residents expressed interest in computer classes.

Recommendations
Firstly, opening hours should be extended until 8 p.m. at least twice a week, and the library should open on Sunday afternoons. Secondly, the library could introduce a monthly programme of events, ideally organised together with local schools and clubs. Finally, the reading room should be modernised, with comfortable chairs, more power sockets and faster internet.

Conclusion
Although digital reading has changed people's habits, the library still has an important role to play in the community. By becoming a meeting place as well as a book collection, it could reverse the fall in visitor numbers.
